It is deliberately not a store skill. Nothing it produces is

name: Skill builder
summary: Turns the open project into a reusable Template Skill, or interrogates the user to build an Analytical Skill.
_theOneIdea: A skill is not a saved project, and every failed attempt at one
fails in the same direction: it rebuilds the video it was made
from. The difference is not the file format, it is whether the
CONTENT has been separated from the STRUCTURE.
Structure is the thing worth keeping: the track stack, the cut
rhythm, the grade, where the captions sit, how the camera behaves.
Content is this footage, these words, this piece of music. A skill
keeps the structure and takes the content as an argument.
So the builder's real job is an interrogation, not a conversion.
`inspect_project_for_skill` lists what is in the project and marks
what looks like content; the agent has to turn each of those into
either a SLOT the user fills in, or an ASSET the skill ships with,
and it has to ask, because only the author knows which.
_trial: Not gated, and it never should be. Charging somebody to make their
own skill out of their own project would be charging them for the
_assets: None. This skill's material is its method, which lives in GUIDE.md
and is read by the agent rather than placed on a timeline.

slots.description: What the NEW skill should make, in one line, for somebody who has not seen this project. 'A 30-second product demo from a screen recording' is a purpose; 'like this video' is not.
Folder name for the new skill: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Derived from the name when left blank.
Copy the project's recurring material (music beds, logos, LUTs) into the skill so it carries them. Turn off when every asset should be supplied per run.

_recipe: Two steps and a conversation between them, and the conversation is
the part that matters. The recipe cannot express 'now ask the user
which of these eleven assets are the subject', so GUIDE.md does,
and the agent is expected to read it. A recipe that ran straight
through without asking would produce exactly the thing this skill
_verify: It checks the one property that makes the output a skill rather
than a saved project: that a manifest with no slots is REFUSED,
that a manifest with slots is written to disk where the app can
read it back, and that a declared asset which is not on disk is
reported as missing rather than passing quietly.
It cannot check that the slots are the RIGHT ones. Nothing can;
